geometry.notes: STRUCTURED PACK, NOT A SOFT WEDGE - this is probably not modelled today. Deep, full-height blunt nose under the saddle that drops into a lobe hugging the seatpost; the body holds its section for most of its run then closes to the rolled tail. Held in shape by four HDPE panels: two small welded side panels, a tapered internal spine along the top, and an external plastic skid plate riveted to the underside with three rivets and Hypalon patches. A rigid UV-stabilised nylon mounting plate is riveted to the top deck and carries two parallel channels (described as skateboard-coping-shaped) for the quick-release pin. The pack barely sags because of this - render it near-rigid.

closure.hardware: single webbing compression strap over the rolled rear end, side-release buckle

details.valve: one-way low-profile air purge valve, front third of the non-drive side panel
details.lightMount: moulded slots at the rear of the mounting plate area for a blinky
details.cord: shock cord laced through the red top daisy loops with a cordlock
details.fabric: polyurethane-coated 210D ripstop nylon, matte

mount.notes: HARDWARE MOUNT, NOT STRAPS. A small forged aluminium clamp bolts to the saddle rails; it carries two U-channels with igus bushings and a tethered steel quick-release pin. The pin drops through one of two channels in the nylon plate riveted to the bag's top deck, giving two fore/aft positions. The two side compression straps loop over horn-shaped protrusions on that same saddle clamp, so load goes into the clamp, not into the fabric. A wide seatpost strap is the only fabric attachment and it sits low on the post. Requires ~16.4 cm of exposed seatpost. NOT compatible with carbon saddle rails, Brooks-style flared rails, dropper posts or suspension posts.

geometry.notes: TWO SEPARATE OBJECTS - almost certainly modelled as one solid today, and it should not be. (1) A radio-frequency-welded dry bag: a near-cylindrical tube, slightly fuller at the rear, that rolls closed at its REAR end. (2) A holster: an open-topped sling of VX21/Cordura with stiff HDPE reinforcing panels in its side walls, which wraps the front two thirds of the drybag from below and leaves the rolled tail proud at the back. The holster carries every strap and every attachment point; the drybag carries none and slides out rearward. The holster's top deck is a flat black textured panel with two rows of red webbing daisy chain and a shock cord.

geometry.notes: The ROAD/GRAVEL full frame bag - cut for tall top tubes and tall head tubes, so it is proportionally deeper front-to-back than the MTB-oriented Ranger and Rifter. Three separate compartments stacked in the panel: a main compartment, a full non-drive-side pocket, and a LOWER compartment of its own along the down tube, each with its own zip. LG and XL add a vertical divider specifically to stop the load bulging into the rider's legs. Full perimeter foam-padded tube sections give it thick soft edges.

products.name: Rifter Frame Bag
products.dims_raw: SM: 349 x 254 mm (L x H); 254 g; NO depth or width figure is published by any source; volume disputed - 3.7 L (BIKEPACKING.com) / 6.0 L (bike-packing.de)
products.dims_note: LENGTH AND HEIGHT ARE SOUND, THE DEPTH IS NOT - flagged low deliberately rather than invented. bike-packing.de's per-size table gives L and H only and states explicitly that no depth or width is published; the maker's own site returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches. The stored wid of 3.8 cm is a catalogue inheritance with no source behind it, and it cannot be reconciled with any published capacity: the 34.9 x 25.4 x 3.8 cm box is only 3.37 L, and a frame bag is closer to a triangular prism (about half its box), i.e. roughly 1.68 L - against a rated 4.5 L here, 3.7 L (BIKEPACKING.com) / 6.0 L (bike-packing.de). Even the lowest published rating would need a depth in the 6-9 cm range, i.e. Ranger-like. I have not substituted a number because none is published and back-computing a dimension from volume is exactly the failure mode this catalogue has been bitten by twice. Treat wid as unknown; if the builder needs a working value, 6.4 cm (the Ranger's) is the defensible placeholder and should be labelled as such. Written as a whole triple. VOLUME also unsettled: bike-packing.de's Rifter volume column is identical to the Ranger's and is almost certainly a copy-paste error; capacity_l keeps the catalogue value, which sits between the two published sets.

geometry.notes: MTB-oriented full frame bag with a TAPERED CONICAL FRONT - it swells toward the head tube for volume and thins toward the seat tube, and it reaches down toward the bottom bracket rather than stopping at the down tube line, which is how it gets its capacity out of a short hardtail triangle with a 1x drivetrain. Stretch Cordura inserts run alongside the main zip, so the top edge bulges when the bag is full instead of straining the zip - a visible, renderable detail.

closure.hardware: water-resistant #10 zip with stretch Cordura inserts either side of the run

zips.note: main compartment, full length of the top edge
full-length non-drive-side pocket

straps.material: adjustable velcro straps running on daisy-chain loops

details.fabric: EcoPac: 100% recycled water-resistant RVX 30 polyester
details.hydrationPort: exit port for a hydration hose or cable
details.divider: vertical divider in the main compartment

mount.notes: The down tube straps run on DAISY-CHAIN LOOPS rather than fixed webbing tabs, so their position along the lower edge is user-set - the bag can be pulled up clear of a shock or dropped toward the bottom bracket. Designed around modern hardtail geometry and 1x drivetrains; the deep front section is what has to be checked against a low-slung gravel down tube.

geometry.notes: HALF-FRAME SLIVER hugging the underside of the top tube, deep at the FRONT and tapering to nothing at the REAR - the dimension drawing shows the height figure measured at the head tube end and the outline sloping away toward the seat tube to a near point. The lower front corner is rounded, the rear edge is raked. It leaves the lower two thirds of the main triangle open, so bottle cages still work under it. Black VX-21 with red accent stitching along the zip line and black textured trim over the top edge.

logo.note: white and red Revelate wordmark low on the drive-side panel

mount.notes: Hangs UNDER the top tube only - it does not reach the down tube, which is the whole difference from the Ranger/Ripio/Rifter and the reason bottle cages stay usable. Two or three wide velcro tabs over the top tube, two forward straps reaching up to 10.2 cm to the head tube, one rear strap reaching up to 10.2 cm diagonally down to the seat tube. Revelate's own drawing carries the note that it is better for the bag to be under a little tension than to hang loose.
